identity: Opening chapter of an English-to-Arabic translated popular-psychology / social-science trade book about embarrassment (الإحراج). Two heading lines sit alone between <NL> markers: the chapter title حقل الألغام الاجتماعي (The Social Minefield) at 0-2 and the section heading الألم الاجتماعي (Social Pain) at 283-284. The body is first-person authorial essay prose by a British writer (Chancery Lane, the Tube, weddings), opening with a domestic anecdote about his daughter Charlotte and a family survey, then arguing through cited authorities — Erving Goffman's طقوس التفاعل, the critic James Wood on a Maupassant sentence, Oliver Burkeman's الترياق, Mark Leary's sociometer — heavily punctuated with rhetorical questions aimed at the reader. Paragraph 980-1060 is a block quotation from Burkeman's book and carries its own first-person 'I'. Register: MSA translationese — long connective-chained periods, frequent sentence-initial فـ / و / لكن / لذا, and short punchy declaratives used as topic sentences and paragraph-closing punchlines.
law: The unit is the orthographic sentence of the printed Arabic translation, i.e. the span that ended in . or ؟. Five working rules. (1) Structural: the token before every <NL> and the final token close a unit by rule; a heading is one unit. (2) A boundary falls wherever a complete predication is followed by another complete, independently assertable predication. In this register a connective at the head of the second clause is NOT evidence against a boundary — MSA translation prose opens sentences with فـ (فهي، فلا، فالتفاعل، فعبارة، فالكاتب، فنحن، فعندما، فثمة، فالأعراس), with و (وحتى، وتوجد، ويعلق، وبصفتنا، ويعد، ولعل، وكأطفال), with لكن، لذا، في الواقع، ولهذا السبب. The real test is whether the following clause makes a NEW assertion or merely completes the current one. (3) Never split inside one syntactic unit, however long: subordinate إذ / إذا / عندما / لأن / ريثما clauses and their apodoses, resumptive relatives (ما يؤدي إلى...), هل...أم alternative questions, fronted adverbials still awaiting their main clause (فعلى عكس...، في المواقف الاجتماعية...), two verbs coordinated under one subject, and quoted or named material embedded as a sentence constituent (عبارة أوه لقد كان هذا محرجا قليلا; سؤال ما أكثر قدرة خارقة تريدين امتلاكها; the Maupassant line; the sticks-and-stones proverb). (4) Every matrix interrogative is its own sentence — هل، ما الذي، كم عدد، ولماذا — and two adjacent interrogatives with no و between them are always two sentences. (5) A short connective that merely glosses or tightly derives from the clause before it stays inside the sentence: أي إنه ... as an appositive gloss, and bare لذا with no فـ / no fronted adverbial after it. Net effect on this document: 67 units over 1206 content tokens, ~18 tokens per sentence, which matches a register that mixes 40-token periods with 5-token rhetorical questions.
reasoning: Hard sites, in order. (11) منذ سنتين attaches BACKWARD to فاجأتني ... بإجابة عن سؤال ('surprised me two years ago'); reading it forward into كنا آنذاك would make آنذاك ('at that time') redundant, so the boundary is at سنتين, not at سؤال. (57, 61) The survey items أسئلة مثل | من صديقاتها | ما الموسيقى التي تحبها | ما النصيحة ... الثانوية run with NO و anywhere between them, which is unparseable as continuous Arabic — some separator was printed. Since all three are full quoted interrogatives, ؟ is likelier than ،, so I split at 57 and 61. Marked lo: this is the one place I split inside material governed by مثل, and it sits in tension with my own rule 3, which is why the confidence is low — if the key says no, the doctrine should read 'enumerated embedded interrogatives take ، not ؟'. Note I did NOT split at 97 (امتلاكها) even though it too is a quoted question, because the main clause visibly continues (بدلا من أن تختار ... قالت), so a break there would strand a fragment. (168) لأن الإحراج يحدث بين الناس is a subordinate clause completing the previous assertion; فلا تستطيع then launches a new second-person claim, so the period goes at الناس. (198) Two bare هل questions with nothing between them — the clearest boundary in the document, and the evidence that ؟ is a terminator here. (229) لا يعتمد الأمر على حكمك فقط is only six tokens but it is a self-standing punchline, and فالتفاعل السلس ... restates the reason; split. (272) ما يؤدي إلى ... النغمة النشاز is a resumptive relative on the Goffman claim, not a new sentence — 243-281 stays one 39-token period. (647) The decisive site: الضرر الذي حدث | في المواقف الاجتماعية يعد الإحراج علامة تحذير. في المواقف الاجتماعية must go FORWARD. Reading it backward gives 'the harm that occurred in social situations', but the example is a physical fall, and the whole rhetorical move is the pivot from physical damage to social damage. Boundary at حدث. (667 vs 672) I did NOT split before أي إنه يدق جرس إنذار: أي here is an appositive gloss on the preceding clause, normally comma-attached in Arabic. I DID split at إنذار, because إذا كنت معرضا ... فأنت مهدد is an unmistakable new conditional sentence, and I did not split at 679 because فأنت is that conditional's apodosis. (714) بل إن هذا الألم أسوأ — بل after a correlative ليس (as at 624, بل يخفي) is intra-sentential, but bare بل إن with a full independent clause reads as 'Indeed, ...' and takes a period; split, med. (744) No split at أبدا: the sticks-and-stones proverb is embedded inside عبارة ... and the fronted فعلى عكس ... still needs its main clause كم عدد المرات, so 726-766 is one 41-token period. (880) The one و I deliberately refused. The document uses BARE لكن to open sentences three times (452 لكن ما يجعل, 800 لكن الالتزام, 848 لكننا) but writes ولكن here — within-document minimal pair, so I read ولكن يجدر بنا as an intra-sentential pivot and let 866-905 run as one 40-token sentence. Lower-confidence omission; if the key splits at الرابع, the doctrine should drop the ولكن/لكن distinction entirely. (990) Same discrimination applied to لذا: I split before لذا وسعيا منه (941) and before لذا فمن شبه المؤكد (1024), because both carry فـ or a fronted adverbial, but NOT before bare لذا ليس لدي شيء أخسره, which is a tight clause-level 'so'. (496, 532, 544, 572) Inside the James Wood passage the translator chains ويستخدم / ويكشف / فالكاتب / فهو / فنحن; each introduces a genuinely new assertion about the writer's technique, so I split at all four. 544 is lo — فالكاتب ... فهو ... could plausibly be one 40-token period, and two consecutive فـ sentences is the shakiest stretch here. I did not split at 555 (ويكشف لنا نحن القراء) because it shares its subject with يدخله. (1118, 1133, 1190) Three و-initial splits in the closing paragraphs, all med: ويعد الإحراج علامة (paragraph-closing punchline), ولعل ارتكاب الخطأ (after the five-token topic sentence ثمة أنواع مختلفة من الإحراج, which announces a topic the next clause does not enumerate, so a comma-join would be odd), and وكأطفال المدارس (a fronted simile heading its own main clause آل المطاف بالضيوف). (978) بالتأكيد closes the paragraph that introduces the Burkeman block quote and is mandatory by the <NL> rule; the quote itself then runs 980-1060 with four internal units.
